description:
Four public Deserialize structs in jmap-jscontact-types derive Hash:
- NameComponent (RFC 9553 §2.2.1.2)
- AddressComponent (RFC 9553 §2.3.1)
- PartialDate (RFC 9553 §2.4.1)
- Timestamp (RFC 9553 §1.4.4)

Adding a `pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>` field
to any of these breaks the derive(Hash) macro because serde_json::Map
does not implement Hash. (It implements PartialEq+Eq via inner BTreeMap,
but BTreeMap+Value does not implement Hash.)

Three resolutions:

A. **Drop Hash on all four.** Smallest code change. Technically API
   breaking — downstream may rely on `NameComponent: Hash`. None of
   the current workspace code uses these as HashMap/HashSet keys
   (verified: only Vec<NameComponent>, Vec<AddressComponent>, and
   field-level usage exists). Pre-1.0 crate; non_exhaustive struct
   already constrains API surface.

B. **Implement Hash manually, skipping the extra field.** Preserves
   the existing Hash derive's intent. Conflicts with auto-derived
   PartialEq+Eq if those include extras (Hash/Eq invariant:
   a == b ⇒ hash(a) == hash(b)). To preserve the invariant we'd
   ALSO need to manually impl PartialEq+Eq to skip extras, which
   means two NameComponents differing only in vendor extras compare
   equal — surprising for a preservation policy.

C. **Exclude these four types from the extras policy.** Deviation
   from the workspace canonical. Vendor extras on a NameComponent
   would silently drop on these four types only. Inconsistent with
   the broader policy goal.

Recommendation: A. The Hash derive on these types appears to be
gratuitous (no callsite needs it) and the Map-cannot-Hash limitation
is well-known. Dropping Hash is the cleanest.

Blocker for: completing JMAP-lbdy.5 cleanly. Current workaround in
JMAP-lbdy.5 commit excludes these four types pending this decision.

Acceptance: chosen resolution applied; PLAN.md updated to record
the policy refinement; if A chosen, downstream consumers
(jmap-contacts-types, etc.) compile cleanly without Hash-of-these
types.
title: Resolve Hash-vs-extras tension on Hash-derived JSContact sub-types
